A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a new genetic model for Ca2+ dependent autophagy and Ca2+ dependent ER-stress in photoreceptor cells in the fly eye.

we identified a novel role for Calphotin in regulating Ca2+ homeoastasis in Drosphila photoreceptors, and that the Ca2+ overload in these cells triggers autophagy and the unfolded protein response (UPR) pathway.
the Drosophilamodel provides a unique opportunity to dissect the molecular mechanisms underlying Ca2+ homeoostasis, ER-stress, and autophagy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Ca2+ overload can induce autophagy and that the autophagy pathway is required for Ca2+ overload-induced photoreceptor degeneration in Drosophilla.
Ca2+ homeostat disruption can lead to degeneration of Drosophila retinal cells.
Ca2+-induced ER-stress and subsequent autophagy can be used as a model to understand the role of these two pathways in neurodegeneration.
